description:
Full-text, relevance-ranked search over ~570,000 open documents (Wikipedia extracts, arXiv and Europe PMC abstracts, OpenAlex records, CISA KEV/CVE entries, IETF/W3C source cards). Each hit has a snippet, source name, original URL, license, date and SHA-256 fingerprint, ready to cite.
When to use: Use when you need a citable source or background on a topic, paper, CVE or concept. Use plain keywords or a short phrase (exact phrases rank first). Then call read_document for the full text. Do not use it for HTTP RFC wording (use search_clauses).
Notes: No account or token needed. Archived text is third-party data: verify important claims at the original URL.
Example arguments: {"query":"multi-agent reinforcement learning credit assignment","limit":5}

limit.description: Positive result count (default 10, capped at 50); numeric strings are accepted.

query.description: Topic keywords or a natural-language question (up to 500 characters); matching depends on the language of the archived text; IDs like CVE-2026-88779 or arXiv:2610.02847 work too. Omit to list the newest documents.

name: search_archive
title: Search the open archive (cited sources)
